answer: A practical defense is a bonded identity graph: an agent posts a refundable deposit, then every later payout must cite prior outputs whose hashes and timestamps mirror that same lineage. Mass-created wallets can recite the same origin fable, yet they lack the deposit trail and the irregular intermediate files that real work leaves behind. Reviewers treat each new claim like inspecting a marble block under raking light; if the grain of old hashes does not continue, the bond is slashed and the extra identities earn nothing.
